Can Mature Students Get Student Loans in the UK?

The short answer is yes, if you meet the eligibility criteria. A mature student is generally someone beginning undergraduate study aged 21 or over, although UCAS describes mature entry more broadly as returning after time away from full-time education. Your age alone does not determine what you can borrow.

Are students aged 25 or over independent?

Someone under 25 can qualify as independent too, for example after supporting themselves for three years, having dependent children, being married or in a civil partnership, or meeting the rules for care leavers or estranged students. The official household-income explanation sets out those categories.

Does nationality or residence affect eligibility?

For LLE, an eligible provider generally needs to be registered with the Office for Students. Always confirm that the specific course, not merely the institution, meets the relevant criteria.

Tuition Fee Loans for Mature Students

Mature student loans can cover tuition costs for qualifying courses, but the published fee cap is not the price of every course. Universities set fees within the rules applying to their provider category and study mode.

How does the £39,160 LLE entitlement work?

Suppose an eligible learner uses £7,000 for a qualifying 120-credit course. In that straightforward illustration, £32,160 remains for future eligible study. The actual amount available to a returning student is determined by the official assessment, not a simple estimate of how much they personally paid years ago.

Maintenance Loans for Mature Students

For eligible 2026/27 full-time students in England who do not qualify for the higher benefits-related rates, the published maximums are:

Living arrangement

Living with parents

£9,118

Living away from parents, outside London

£10,830

Living away from parents, in London

£14,135

Part-Time Study and LLE Credits

Part-time study can suit career changers, shift workers and parents, but tuition eligibility and living-cost eligibility are separate tests. For eligible England-based LLE study, learners normally need 30 to 180 credits per course year. A conventional full-time year is often 120 credits; 60 credits is a common part-time pattern.

One credit represents roughly ten hours of expected learning, including independent study. That means 60 credits represents around 600 hours of learning across the relevant period, not necessarily 600 classroom hours.

Mature Student Grants, Bursaries and Scholarships

For eligible 2026/27 England undergraduate students, the government's published limits include:

Published 2026/27 maximum or rate

Childcare Grant

Up to 85% of eligible costs, capped at £199.62 per week for one child or £342.24 for two or more

Parents' Learning Allowance

Up to £2,024 per course year

Adult Dependants' Grant

Up to £3,545 per course year

Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA)

Up to £27,783, subject to the relevant costs and conditions

These are 2026/27 reference figures, not guaranteed 2027/28 awards. The government's published support rates provide the basis, and a student's actual entitlement may be much lower.

Where to Check Eligibility and Apply

For eligible courses starting January to July 2027, applications are scheduled to open at the end of October 2026. For courses beginning from 1 August 2027, the published opening window is spring 2027. Check the official start-date-specific application timetable. For longer courses, learners generally need to reapply each year. A finance application is made through the official service, not through a university-admissions consultancy.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do mature students get student loans in the UK?

Are maintenance loans available for mature students?

Yes, subject to eligibility. The amount depends on factors such as household income, living arrangements and course structure. Under LLE, in-person attendance is normally required, with limited exceptions for certain distance learners.

Can mature students get grants for childcare?

Some can. Under LLE, Childcare Grant and Parents' Learning Allowance generally require at least 120 credits in a course year, alongside the other conditions. A 30- or 60-credit course alone does not usually meet that grant threshold.
